A.notes: A has a clear brick/courtyard idea and carries it through the hero, project imagery and plans, with a restrained mood that fits the brief. The typography and layout are clean, but the overall structure feels more familiar than distinctive, and the scroll-frame strip shows mostly ordinary scrolling rather than motion doing conceptual work. Automated checks are solid, with reduced-motion, keyboard reachability and no contrast failures.

B.notes: B has the stronger point of view: the brick-course lines, monumental serif typography and boxed 'courtyard' motif make one coherent identity across the whole page. The project presentation is especially well crafted, with plans and elevations consistently drawn and composed on both desktop and mobile. From the scroll-frame strip, motion appears minimal or mostly standard scrolling/reveals, so I would not score that axis highly despite the strong visual design; accessibility checks still pass cleanly.

raw.why: B is the more distinctive and fully realized response, with stronger typography and a more memorable architectural signature while still meeting the brief cleanly.
